oregon-trail-cd.garden_page_title: The Oregon Trail CD - Macintosh Garden
copyright: Disclaimer: Macintosh Garden does not claim rights to any software on the site. To the best of our knowledge, these titles have been discontinued by their publishers. If you know otherwise, please contact us and we will remove them accordingly. Thank you for your attention.
oregon-trail-cd.download_label: DL #1 (2009-12-10): OregonTrail1.2.sit_.bin (45.79 MB), an image of the Mac CD
oregon-trail-cd.description: The CD-ROM edition of The Oregon Trail, with digitized photos, spoken guide books and music. Lead a wagon party from Independence, Missouri, to Oregon's Willamette Valley in 1848. The original 1971 game is by Don Rawitsch, Bill Heinemann and Paul Dillenberger. Produced by Craig Copley and Wayne Studer. Programmed by Joan Clarke, Tom Naughton, Brian Nesse and Steve Splinter. Art by Dave Denninger, Charolyn Kapplinger and Mike Tschimperle. Music and sound by Larry Phenow.
oregon-trail-cd.notes: copyright[0] is the 'vers' 1 resource. The authors come from the credits screen (TEXT 200), which also names the testers, the voice actors, the singers, the choir and the team of Oregon Trail 1.0 for Macintosh. The Garden lists the publisher as The Learning Company, which bought MECC later; the CD says MECC. We copy the app and 'Oregon Data' off the raw HFS image and leave out the HyperCard user's guide.

shufflepuck-cafe.title: Shufflepuck Café
copyright: Disclaimer: Macintosh Garden does not claim rights to any software on the site. To the best of our knowledge, these titles have been discontinued by their publishers. If you know otherwise, please contact us and we will remove them accordingly. Thank you for your attention.
shufflepuck-cafe.download_label: DL #3 (2016-04-22): ZIP file added for use with emulators. Disk image used: 'Shufflepuck Cafe (cheats).dsk'.
shufflepuck-cafe.description: You [are] thrust into [a] rough and tumble space bar, clearly the outsider, forced to prove yourself in a true game of wits and agility: computer air hockey. It was a simple game for simple times: a handful of wacky alien characters, mild nudity, and an animated screen crack when your opponent scored. Ah to go back for one more round.
shufflepuck-cafe.description_credit: Quoted on the Macintosh Garden page from: Putney, Dean "Nostalgia: Shufflepuck Café", Cult of Mac (http://cultofmac.com/nostalgia-shufflepuck-cafe/6399)
shufflepuck-cafe.notes: The hosted application matches 'Shufflepuck Cafe (cheats).dsk' in SPuck.zip byte for byte. It does not match the 1.0 disk or the 'nude' disk. The page calls this build "Version 14C: A near-final pre-release build, with a cheat menu and zero copy protection", and says that its "about box, and title screen copyright" differ from 1.0. The application has no 'vers' resource and no copyright text in its string resources. The copyright is drawn in PICT images, which we could not render, so it is not recorded here. Read it from the About box or title screen in the running game. The page shows no uploader credit. The other agent must confirm the download file and version.
